name: Slack
summary: A Slack app can be created and installed in your own workspace in minutes. Installing into other workspaces requires turning on public distribution. A Slack Marketplace listing is optional but adds a review that takes weeks.

verdict.label: Moderate
verdict.headline: Working in your workspace in 15 minutes. Other workspaces need public distribution, and the Marketplace adds weeks.

approvalWait.appliesWhen: only if you list in the Slack Marketplace; public distribution itself has no review

timeline.summary: No wait to distribute; Marketplace review is optional

agent: Generate an app manifest (YAML/JSON) with scopes, redirect URLs and event subscriptions
Choose bot vs user token scopes for your use case
Exercise the oauth.v2.access exchange once you paste a client_id
human: Sign in to api.slack.com and create the app from the manifest
Install into a workspace where you're an admin (or ask an admin)
Turn on public distribution (requires an https redirect URL)
Submit to the Marketplace if you want a listing

steps.title: Create app from a manifest
steps.detail: api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From a manifest. The manifest captures scopes and redirect URLs, so the agent can write it for you.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs. Must be https for public distribution. Localhost works only for single-workspace dev.

steps.title: Install to your workspace
steps.detail: This gives you a bot token (xoxb-) immediately, which is enough for internal agents.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution → remove hard-coded info → Activate. There's no review; any workspace can now install via /oauth/v2/authorize.

steps.title: (Optional) Slack Marketplace review
steps.detail: Requires privacy policy, support page, landing page, and a review of scopes and security practices.

evidence.note: Slack lists requirements but no SLA; duration is from community reports

requirements.item: Workspace where you can install apps
requirements.note: Many corporate workspaces require admin approval for new apps.

scopes.name: im:history / groups:history
scopes.purpose: Read DMs and private channels, which reviewers scrutinize

endpoints.refreshTokens: Only if token rotation is enabled
endpoints.tokenLifetime: No expiry by default · 12h with rotation

evidence.note: OIDC discovery exists but covers Sign in with Slack only; the v2 bot flow isn't listed in it

blockers.symptom: 'Something went wrong when authorizing this app' in another workspace

blockers.cause: The target workspace restricts app installs.
blockers.fix: Users can request approval; a workspace admin approves under Manage apps.

gotchas.title: OIDC discovery ≠ the bot OAuth flow
gotchas.detail: slack.com/.well-known/openid-configuration describes 'Sign in with Slack' (openid scopes) only. Bot installs use /oauth/v2/authorize, which isn't in the discovery doc.

gotchas.title: Rate limits on history methods for non-Marketplace apps
gotchas.detail: Slack has tightened conversations.history rate limits for commercially distributed apps that aren't Marketplace-approved. Check the current limits before you rely on reading history.

tested.result: 200, authorize=/openid/connect/authorize, 3 scopes (openid, email, profile), no registration_endpoint
200 HTML (Slack renders a page and doesn't return an OAuth error to a redirect)

uncertainties: The exact rate-limit numbers for non-Marketplace apps should be confirmed on the current Slack changelog.
